subject: NovumCare private deployment — onramp selection and recommendation
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Ayesha Singh <ays@novumcare.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: NovumCare private deployment — onramp selection and recommendation

Hi Ayesha,

Great to meet earlier — thanks for the time. Per the call I sketched three onramp patterns for connecting NovumCare's VPCs/on-prem sites to Redwood Private (private control plane + inference dataplane). Before we lock a recommendation we need a couple of constraints from your side:

- Which accounts/regions will be in-scope for the pilot (single AWS account vs multi-account; region names)?
- Any procurement timeline for dedicated connectivity (Direct Connect / colocation)?
- Bandwidth SLA expectations (e.g., sustained 500 Mbps vs bursty 2 Gbps)?
- Security constraints: are interface endpoints blocked? is cross-account peering prohibited by policy?

High-level options we discussed (short):
1) VPC Peering — simplest for same-region, single-account or small multi-account set. Low protocol overhead but not transitive and can be operationally heavy for many peers.
2) PrivateLink (AWS Interface Endpoint) — hides our endpoints in your VPC; good for least-privilege access and per-service allowlists; costs for ENIs/NLB and per-hour endpoints.
3) Site-to-site VPN (IPSec) — quick to stand up, works for on-prem and cloud, but higher latency/less predictable throughput than direct/private options.

I can turn these into a short recommendation with cost/latency tradeoffs if you confirm the constraints above.

Best,
Marcus

Marcus — thanks, useful summary. Answers inline:

- Pilot will be single AWS account initially (us-west-2), but we expect to add eu-west-1 for DR in Q4.
- Procurement: we can request Direct Connect, but earliest turnaround is ~10-12 weeks.
- Bandwidth: pilot needs sustained ~300 Mbps with occasional bursts to 1 Gbps.
- Security: due to our compliance posture we prefer no direct peering into our primary production VPCs (controlled by central platform). Private endpoints are allowed but must go through our security review; public-facing endpoints are a hard no.

Also attaching our network constraints spreadsheet (high level): we use overlapping /16s across some edge accounts and have a central firewall that controls egress. NetOps asked me to get a clear recommendation on which pattern minimizes operational changes on their side.

Ayesha Singh

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-23T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: RE: NovumCare private deployment — onramp selection and recommendation

On Tue, May 23, 2027 at 09:58 AM Ayesha Singh <ays@novumcare.com> wrote:
> Pilot will be single AWS account initially (us-west-2), but we expect to add eu-west-1 for DR in Q4.
> Procurement: Direct Connect earliest turnaround is ~10-12 weeks.
> Bandwidth: pilot needs sustained ~300 Mbps with occasional bursts to 1 Gbps.
> Security: prefer no direct peering into primary production VPCs. Private endpoints allowed after review.

Thanks — quick analysis (short, focused for Marcus to send back):

VPC Peering
- Pros: minimal per-request latency; native routing.
- Cons: Not transitive (would need peering mesh if we expand to multiple VPCs/regions). Because NovumCare's central team prohibits direct peering into prod VPCs, peering is unlikely unless they create a dedicated connectivity VPC.

PrivateLink (Interface Endpoint)
- Pros: Fits NovumCare's security stance (no route table injection into prod VPCs), cross-account access via endpoint service, granular IAM + SG control. Works well for multi-account expansion.
- Cons: Slightly higher avg latency vs peering (encapsulation to NLB), per-endpoint hourly and data charges. Requires us to run an NLB/ENI in a service VPC.

Site-to-site VPN
- Pros: Fast to spin up for pilot; works for on-prem and cloud; no need to change routing inside prod VPCs if NAT'd appropriately.
- Cons: IPSec throughput/latency variability; operational overhead for tunnel monitoring and rekeying; not ideal long-term for predictable high-throughput inference.

Recommended phased approach (my take):
1) Pilot: PrivateLink for control + API traffic (model selection, auth) + a secured S2S VPN for bulk inference flows as a low-friction proof-of-concept.
2) Post-pilot (after throughput/latency validation): move data-plane to either Direct Connect or a dedicated peering VPC (if NovumCare can stand up a connectivity VPC and policy permits) for lower and more predictable latency.

I'll draft a short PoC checklist (security review items, test vectors, perf targets) and an updated cost note.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Network Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Ayesha Singh <ays@novumcare.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-24T08:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: NovumCare private deployment — onramp selection and recommendation

Ayesha — based on your constraints and Kim's notes, here's a concise recommendation and next steps. I've attached a simple topology diagram and a draft SOW for the pilot. Attachments: redwood-novumcare-ingress-drawing.png, milestone-sow-v1.pdf.

Recommendation (short):
- Short-term (pilot, 2–4 weeks):
  - Control plane & management traffic: AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoint pointing to Redwood-svc NLB in our service VPC). This keeps everything inside NovumCare's VPCs and aligns with the "no direct peering into prod" policy.
  - Data plane (inference payloads): Site-to-site IPSec VPN from NovumCare edge firewall → our gateway. Use two tunnels for HA. We'll cap cipher suites per your security review. Expect slightly higher p99 latency here but sufficient for initial SLA.

- Medium-term (post-pilot):
  - If throughput and latency are insufficient, migrate the data plane to Direct Connect (preferred) or a dedicated connectivity VPC with controlled peering into an aggregation VPC. Direct Connect gives consistent bandwidth; peering reduces hop count but needs a connectivity VPC to respect your policy.

Operational notes / items needed from NovumCare:
1) Confirm us-west-2 account id(s) and exact VPC CIDR(s) (we need non-overlapping ranges for PrivateLink).
2) Provide contact and access for NetOps to validate IPsec tunnel setup (preferably a test edge appliance).
3) Approve initial perf targets: 300 Mbps sustained, p95 latency target <= 120 ms (round-trip from NovumCare edge to Redwood inference node).
4) Security review kickoff (I'll include our SOC2 pack and network hardening checklist).

Proposed PoC timeline (high level):
- Week 0: Kickoff + exchange of network artifacts (ours + yours)
- Week 1: PrivateLink endpoint provisioning + IPsec tunnel config
- Week 2: Smoke tests, auth validation, small-volume inference tests
- Week 3: Load test to 300 Mbps sustained; capture p50/p95/p99; iterate

Cost note: PrivateLink endpoints + data processing fees for pilot will be modest (low hundreds per endpoint / month + per-GB). IPsec egress charges apply per cloud provider. We'll provide a more detailed estimate once account details are shared.

Next steps — can we book a 45-minute network validation call this week? I can bring Kim and a runtime engineer to walk your NetOps through the diagram.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
